title: Emrys and the Veil
premise: Tamsin Okafor poisons herself professionally by day and keeps the ledgers of the Veilwrights' Guild—a covenant-brokerage between the human realm and the fading fae Otherworld—by night. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, she discovers her guild has been quietly selling pieces of the covenant to Lord Cassian Vey, a usurper who means to sever the realms entirely and rule a world with no magic but his own. Tamsin must gather the scattered signatories of the original covenant—some grateful, some vengeful—and reforge it at the Veil's heart before Vey's armies reach the free cities. She succeeds only by offering the one thing no one else can: her trained immunity, absorbing the covenant's death-curse meant for all signatories, and in doing so becomes the living seal between realms—no longer a taster of poison, but a keeper of balance.
about_author: Kestrel Quintana is a former line cook turned archivist who claims they learned everything about power from watching who was allowed to eat first. They write fantasy about people whose jobs are considered invisible until the world breaks.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A routine poisoning at the royal table introduces her double life: food-taster by day, ledger-keeper for the Veilwrights' Guild by night. We learn the guild trades in impossible things—bargains, borders, borrowed luck. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; Tamsin belongs everywhere and nowhere.

chapters.title: Ledgers of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the guildhall beneath the city, she audits entries that shouldn't exist—including payments made in starlight to an unnamed buyer. Her mentor, Guildmaster Sorrel, deflects her questions. Emotional beat: unease; the first crack in her trust in the institution that raised her.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The border wards fail at moonrise; every star vanishes at once. Panic floods the capital as the Veil frays visibly overhead. Sorrel presses a sealed ledger into Tamsin's hands and tells her to run. Emotional beat: terror and vertigo—the world's rules breaking in real time.

chapters.title: What Sorrel Knew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, fleeing through collapsing streets. Assassins bearing Vey's crest hunt the ledger. She learns Sorrel sold covenant-segments to Vey before dying or disappearing—she can't tell which. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with grief; the guild that gave her belonging also broke the world.

chapters.title: The Free City of Harrowgate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She reaches Harrowgate, where refugees and fae exiles crowd together uneasily. She meets Brannic, a disgraced ward-smith, and Yew, a half-fae smuggler who recognizes the ledger. Emotional beat: wary first sparks of found family among strangers.

chapters.title: Signatories, Scattered
chapters.summary: Yew's POV. The original covenant had seven signatories across both realms; three are dead, two are hiding, one is Vey himself. Yew explains what the covenant actually does: it is the Veil's skeleton. Emotional beat: dawning scale—this isn't politics, it's cosmology.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Summons
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Vey's herald offers amnesty for the ledger and reveals he knows her name, her guild, her immunity training. Refusal means Harrowgate burns first. Emotional beat: cold fear sharpening into defiance—justice won't come from thrones.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Borrowed Luck
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. To reach the first hidden signatory, the trio must cross the Mire of Small Debts, where every favor ever owed comes due. Brannic pays with his smith's oath. Emotional beat: sacrifice establishing trust; Brannic chooses these people over his old life.

chapters.title: The Signatory Who Hates Her
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Signatory Maerin, an exiled fae noble, blames human guildkeepers for the covenant's decay and nearly kills Tamsin before reading the ledger. What's inside changes her mind: Vey's payments were signed in Sorrel's hand—with Tamsin's countersignature forged. Emotional beat: rage transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Armies on the March
chapters.summary: Yew's POV. Vey's legions move on the free cities; refugee columns choke the roads. Yew runs smuggling routes into evacuation lines, confronting his own history of profiting from desperation. Emotional beat: guilt and redemption—he starts giving away what he used to sell.

chapters.title: The Drowned Archive
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Beneath a sunken library, the second signatory guards the covenant's original text—which names a final clause: the Veil can be reforged only by someone who has survived every poison of both realms. Tamsin realizes her immunity was never a job qualification. It was preparation. Emotional beat: revelation reframing her whole life.

chapters.title: What Was Done to Me
chapters.summary: Maerin's POV. Flashback threads reveal the guild deliberately raised foundling tasters as potential covenant-vessels. Tamsin's 'belonging' was engineered. She takes it with terrible calm. Emotional beat: grief for a self that may have been designed—but choosing her own use for it anyway.

chapters.title: The Traitor Among Us
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. One of their number has been feeding Vey their route. Evidence points to Yew; Tamsin defends him; the real traitor is revealed to be a fae shadow wearing a companion's face. Emotional beat: tested loyalty—found family survives its first real fracture.

chapters.title: Vey's Court of Ash
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, captured. In Vey's war camp she sees his prize: a caged shard of the Veil, which he feeds captured fae to sustain his own magic. He offers her a place—immunity makes her valuable, not disposable. Emotional beat: temptation offered sincerely, refused clearly.

chapters.title: Escape Written in Ledger-Script
chapters.summary: Yew's POV. The rescue hinges on Tamsin's guild training: she rewrites the camp's contract-wards from memory, voiding Vey's claim on the shard long enough to shatter part of it. They escape with a fragment and a plan. Emotional beat: competence as liberation; her invisible skills save everyone.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Fragment
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The shattered shard's backlash curses every remaining signatory with slow dissolution. The reforging must happen within nine days—at the Veil's heart, behind Vey's advancing lines. Emotional beat: ticking clock; despair held at bay by stubbornness.

chapters.title: Mustering the Broken
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Refugees, deserters, fae exiles, and two recovered signatories gather at Harrowgate—not an army, a covenant. Each contributes a piece: oaths, skills, names. Emotional beat: belonging made literal; the found family becomes a founding family.

chapters.title: The March Through the Dark
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Under a starless sky, the covenant-company slips past Vey's siege lines toward the Veil's heart. Skirmishes cost them Maerin's mortal shell—she continues as pure fae-fire, dimming. Emotional beat: mourning while moving; love expressed as forward motion.

chapters.title: The Heart of the Veil
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the covenant-stone, the reforging requires a vessel to hold the death-curse meant for all signatories. Vey arrives with his army and the last shard. Battle ignites around the stone. Emotional beat: terrible clarity—Tamsin knows what she came to do.

chapters.title: Every Poison Ever Drunk
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. She drinks the covenant-curse as she once drank poison at the king's table—one sip at a time, trained immunity against cosmic malice. Vey, denied his severed world, is unmade when the reforged Veil rejects him. Stars reignite overhead. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with near-death; she falls as the sky relights.

chapters.title: The Living Seal
chapters.summary: Yew's POV. Tamsin wakes changed—bound to the Veil, able to feel both realms' edges. The free cities stand; the guild is dissolved and remade under new, honest ledgers with her name as first keeper. Emotional beat: exhaustion, tenderness, the strange peace of being needed without being owned.

chapters.title: A Table Set for Everyone
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, coda. Seasons later, she hosts a harvest meal in the rebuilt guildhall—signatories, refugees, fae and human alike, eating first together. She tastes each dish out of habit, finds nothing poisoned, and laughs. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution; justice outside the law, belonging chosen freely, family that fed itself into being.
